docs.title: roman-epsf
docs.text: roman-epsf provides effective Point Spread Function (ePSF) modeling algorithms tailored for the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Wide Field Instrument (WFI). It provides two pluggable, high-precision algorithms for constructing empirical and semi-analytical ePSFs from calibrated Roman WFI exposures.

docs.title: About NASA Roman & the Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey
docs.text:
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is NASA's new flagship observatory, engineered to explore the infrared universe with unprecedented speed and precision. Its primary imaging camera, the Wide Field Instrument (WFI), combines 18 Sensor Chip Assemblies (SCAs) totaling 300 megapixels to yield a 0.281 deg² field of view—roughly 100 times that of the Hubble Space Telescope at comparable resolution (0.11 arcsec/pixel).

A cornerstone community initiative of Roman is the Galactic Bulge Time Domain Survey (GBTDS). By continuously monitoring ~2 square degrees in the dense, dust-obscured Milky Way bulge with ~12-minute sampling over six 62-day seasons in the near-infrared, the GBTDS will detect tens of thousands of exoplanets via the transiting method, discover stellar oscillations, and measure billions of stellar positions.

docs.title: The TRExS Project: Transits in the Roman Galactic EXoplanet Survey
docs.text:
TRExS (Transits in the Roman Galactic EXoplanet Survey) is a Wide Field Science initiative and a Roman Cycle 1 designed to maximize the transit science return from Roman's GBTDS. While the GBTDS is nominally optimized for gravitational microlensing, its high-cadence time-series imaging of hundreds of millions of stars toward the Galactic Center makes it one of the most powerful transiting exoplanet surveys ever conceived.

Key pillars of TRExS include: - Massive Exoplanet Yields: TRExS is predicted to discover between ~100,000 transiting exoplanets, expanding the catalog of known exoplanets by orders of magnitude compared to Kepler and TESS. - Statistical Demographics of Rare Systems: The enormous sample size places stringent demographic constraints on intrinsically rare planetary architectures, ultra-short-period planets, planets orbiting evolved or giant stars, and brown dwarf companions. - Galactic Depth & Diversity: Probing deep through the Galactic disk into the inner bulge, TRExS observes stars across diverse stellar populations, metallicities, and Galactic environments, mapping how planet occurrence varies throughout the Milky Way. - Near-Infrared Atmospheres: Leveraging Roman's near-infrared bandpass (WFI F146 and companion filters), TRExS enables direct atmospheric detection and thermal emission measurements (e.g., secondary eclipses and phase curves) for thousands of transiting giant planets at a population level. - Survey Synergy: By pairing transit discoveries with microlensing detections in the same survey footprint, Roman and TRExS will establish a unified census of planetary systems spanning orbital separations from <0.1 AU out to free-floating planets.

Within the TRExS software ecosystem, roman-epsf generates the high-fidelity empirical and semi-analytical effective PSF (ePSF) models required by roman-lcs for precision crowded-field photometry.

docs.title: Modeling Methods
docs.text:
Module Algorithm Best suited for roman_epsf.photutils photutils.psf.EPSFBuilder — iterative stamp-stacking & sub-pixel centroiding Bright, isolated stars; high-fidelity core modeling; global and spatial grid ePSF maps. roman_epsf.psfmachine Polar B-spline modeling (NumPy/SciPy, inspired by PSFMachine) Large star samples in crowded fields; faint or moderately blended stars; compact parameter storage.

Both methods share the roman_epsf.star_selection module for isolation filtering, flux-percentile selection, and Data Quality (DQ) bitmasking.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: roman-epsf requires Python ≥ 3.11.

docs.title: User Installation with pip
docs.text:
Install the latest release from PyPI:

pip install roman-epsf

To include Roman Data Quality (dq) handling from roman-datamodels:

pip install "roman-epsf[dq]"

Or install from a local clone:

git clone https://github.com/jorgemarpa/roman-epsf.git
cd roman-epsf
pip install -e ".[dq]"

docs.title: Development Installation with uv
docs.text:
We recommend uv for development. When developing across the TRExS Roman toolchain, roman-epsf can link to a local editable copy of roman-cuts:

# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/jorgemarpa/roman-epsf.git
cd roman-epsf

# Sync environment with all development and optional extras
uv sync --all-extras

# Run tests
uv run pytest -v

# Run linting and type checking
uv run ruff check .
uv run mypy src/

# Build and preview documentation locally
uv run mkdocs serve

docs.title: 1. Star Selection
docs.text:
Select suitable PSF stars from a catalog and extract background-subtracted cutouts:

from roman_epsf import select_stars, extract_star_cutouts

# Filter stars by isolation and flux distribution
stars_df = select_stars(
    catalog=catalog,              # pd.DataFrame with coordinates
    image_shape=image.shape,      # (ny, nx)
    cutout_size=25,
    flux_percentile_range=(60, 99),
    min_sep_factor=1.2,           # Isolation radius factor
    gwcs=wcs,                     # Optional GWCS if catalog contains RA/Dec
)

# Extract calibrated star cutouts with Data Quality masking
nddata, cutouts, stars_df, bkg_std = extract_star_cutouts(
    image=image,
    dq=dq,
    stars_df=stars_df,
    cutout_size=25,
    background="global",          # "global", "2d", or None
)

docs.title: Global ePSF from an Exposure
docs.text:
from roman_epsf import build_global_epsf, save_epsf, load_epsf

# Build global ePSF model across an exposure
epsf, fitted_stars, stars_df = build_global_epsf(
    image=image,
    catalog=catalog,
    dq=dq,
    cutout_size=25,
    oversampling=3,
    background="global",
)

# Save to standard FITS format
save_epsf(epsf, "roman_epsf.fits", extra_header={"FILTER": "F146", "SCA": 2})

# Reload from FITS
loaded_epsf, header = load_epsf("roman_epsf.fits")

docs.title: Spatially Varying Grid ePSF
docs.text:
from roman_epsf import build_grid_epsf, save_epsf

# Build a 4x4 spatial grid of ePSF models across the detector
grid = build_grid_epsf(
    image=image,
    catalog=catalog,
    dq=dq,
    n_grid_x=4,
    n_grid_y=4,
    cutout_size=25,
    oversampling=3,
)

# Save multi-cell grid model to FITS
save_epsf(grid, "roman_grid_epsf.fits")

docs.title: Multi-Epoch ePSF
docs.text:
from roman_epsf import build_multiepoch_epsf

# Build composite ePSF from multiple dithered cutouts
# cutout_list: list of dicts with keys 'data', 'dq', 'cutout_center', 'origin'
epsf, fitted_stars = build_multiepoch_epsf(cutout_list, oversampling=3)

docs.title: 3. psfmachine Method — Polar B-Spline Modeling
docs.text:
The polar B-spline method represents the PSF using continuous 2D radial and azimuthal B-splines, providing stable convergence even in dense star fields:

from roman_epsf import select_stars
from roman_epsf.psfmachine import (
    build_pixel_arrays,
    fit_epsf,
    evaluate_epsf,
    save_model,
    load_model,
)

# Select stars (can include fainter sources)
stars_df = select_stars(catalog, image.shape, cutout_size=25, flux_percentile_range=(20, 98))

# Assemble normalized pixel coordinate arrays
dx, dy, norm_flux, star_idx = build_pixel_arrays(image, dq, stars_df, cutout_size=25)

# Fit continuous polar B-spline model
model = fit_epsf(
    dx=dx,
    dy=dy,
    norm_flux=norm_flux,
    n_r_knots=12,
    n_phi_knots=15,
    rmin=0.5,
    rmax=12.0,
)

# Evaluate on an oversampled grid for photometry
psf_array = evaluate_epsf(model, cutout_size=25, oversampling=4)

# Save compact B-spline weights to FITS
save_model(model, "roman_psm_weights.fits")
loaded_model, header = load_model("roman_psm_weights.fits")

docs.title: FITS Serialization Formats
docs.text: roman-epsf outputs self-documenting FITS files compatible with standard astronomy tooling: - Single ePSF: PrimaryHDU containing the 2D oversampled PSF image, with keywords OVERSMPX, OVERSMPY, ORIGIN_X, ORIGIN_Y, and EPSFGRID=False. - Grid ePSF: PrimaryHDU metadata + one ImageHDU per spatial grid cell (CELL_IY_IX) + BinTableHDU (GRID_GEOM) storing cell centers and star counts (EPSFGRID=True). - PSFMachine Spline: PrimaryHDU metadata + ImageHDU "WEIGHTS" (B-spline coefficients) + ImageHDU "R_KNOTS" (radial knot locations).

docs.title: build_multiepoch_epsf
docs.text:
build_multiepoch_epsf(
    cutout_list: list[dict],
    oversampling: int = 3,
    maxiters: int = 5,
    snr_threshold: float = 5.0,
    min_snr_pixels: int = 5,
    **epsf_kwargs,

Build an ePSF model from multi-epoch cutouts of a single star.

Each epoch provides a slightly different sub-pixel sampling of the PSF. The cutouts are wrapped into photutils.psf.EPSFStar objects and combined by EPSFBuilder.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default cutout_list list of dict

Each dict must contain:

  • 'data': 2D np.ndarray science cutout (background not yet subtracted; a local sigma-clipped median is removed per epoch).
  • 'dq': 2D DQ array or None.
  • 'cutout_center': (x, y) star position within the cutout (0-indexed).
  • 'origin': (x, y) cutout origin in detector pixel coordinates.
required oversampling int

EPSFBuilder oversampling factor. Default 3.

3 maxiters int

Maximum EPSFBuilder iterations. Default 5.

5 snr_threshold float

Minimum per-pixel SNR; epochs with fewer than min_snr_pixels valid pixels above this threshold are skipped.

5.0 min_snr_pixels int

Minimum valid pixels above snr_threshold to include an epoch.

5 **epsf_kwargs

Additional keyword arguments forwarded to EPSFBuilder.

{}

Returns:

Name Type Description epsf_model EPSFModel

Fitted multi-epoch ePSF model.

fitted_stars EPSFStars

Per-epoch star cutouts with updated centroid fits.

docs.title: PSFMachine Polar B-Spline Builder
docs.text: Polar B-spline ePSF modeling for Roman WFI detectors.

docs.title: roman_epsf.psfmachine.builder
docs.text:
PSFMachine-style polar B-spline ePSF construction using pure NumPy / SciPy.

Methodology (Hedges et al. 2021)
  1. Extract cutout stamps around a selection of stars.
  2. Normalise each stamp's pixel values by the catalog flux estimate for the corresponding star.
  3. Record the per-pixel offset from the star position in detector pixels (delta_col, delta_row).
  4. Convert to polar coordinates (r, phi) and fit a B-spline model on the polar grid to the assembled normalised-flux vs. position data.
  5. Evaluate the fitted model on any oversampled pixel grid.

The star-selection step deliberately uses looser criteria than the photutils path (fainter stars are accepted because flux normalisation removes the brightness dependence).

docs.title: PSFMachineModel dataclass
docs.text:
Container for a fitted B-spline ePSF model.

Supports two coordinate systems controlled by the coords attribute:

"polar" Tensor product of radial clamped B-splines × periodic azimuthal B-splines, with a radial-only core inside cut_r. Uses r_knots for the radial basis.

"cartesian" Full 2D tensor product of clamped B-splines along the column and row axes, with sqrt-spaced knots inside cut_r for higher resolution at the PSF core. Uses r_knots for the column axis and row_knots for the row axis.

The :meth:evaluate method automatically dispatches to the correct design matrix based on coords.

Attributes:

Name Type Description weights ndarray

Fitted B-spline coefficients.

r_knots ndarray

Radial knot positions for polar mode, or column-axis knot positions for Cartesian mode.

n_r_knots int

Number of radial / column knots.

n_phi_knots int

Number of azimuthal knots (polar mode). 0 for Cartesian mode.

rmin float

Inner radial limit in detector pixels (polar mode).

rmax float

Outer radial / domain half-width limit in detector pixels.

cut_r float

Polar: radius below which only radial terms are used. Cartesian: transition radius from sqrt-spaced to linear knots.

degree int

B-spline degree (default 3 = cubic).

n_stars int

Number of stars used to build the model.

n_pixels int

Total number of valid pixels used to fit the model.

coords str

Coordinate system: "polar" (default) or "cartesian".

row_knots ndarray or None

Row-axis knot positions for Cartesian mode. None for polar mode.

docs.title: evaluate
docs.text:
evaluate(
    delta_col: ndarray,
    delta_row: ndarray,
    clip_negative: bool = False,
) -> ndarray

Evaluate the ePSF model at arbitrary (delta_col, delta_row) offsets.

Automatically dispatches to the polar or Cartesian design matrix based on :attr:coords. When :attr:log_fit is True (the default), raw model outputs are in log₁₀ space and are transformed back to flux via 10 ** val before returning.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default delta_col ndarray

1D arrays of pixel offsets from the star centre (detector pixels).

required delta_row ndarray

1D arrays of pixel offsets from the star centre (detector pixels).

required clip_negative bool

Set negative model values to zero after evaluation. Default False (unnecessary when log_fit=True since 10^x > 0).

False

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

Evaluated normalised flux at each supplied position.

docs.title: build_pixel_arrays
docs.text:
build_pixel_arrays(
    image: ndarray,
    dq: ndarray | None,
    selected_stars: DataFrame,
    cutout_size: int,
    flux_col: str | None = None,
    background: str | None = "local",
    sigma_clip_bg: float = 3.0,
    norm_mode: str = "catalog",
) -> tuple[ndarray, ndarray, ndarray, ndarray]

Assemble per-pixel offset and normalised-flux arrays from star cutouts.

For each star in selected_stars a cutout_size × cutout_size stamp is extracted, background subtracted (optionally), normalised by the catalog flux estimate, and flattened. All stars are concatenated into 1D arrays ready for :func:fit_epsf.

The star-selection can be looser than for the photutils path: fainter and less isolated stars are acceptable because flux normalisation removes the brightness dependence.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default image ndarray

2D background-subtracted science image (detector pixels).

required dq ndarray or None

2D data-quality array. Bits DO_NOT_USE and SATURATED are masked when roman-datamodels is available; otherwise all non-zero DQ values are masked.

required selected_stars DataFrame

Catalog rows with columns x_pix, y_pix, and a flux column (auto-detected from flux_col or common catalog column names).

required cutout_size int

Side length of each star stamp (pixels).

required flux_col str or None

Catalog column containing the flux normalisation value. If None, the first matching column among ['segment_flux', 'psf_flux', 'aper_flux', 'kron_flux', 'flux'] is used.

None background ('local', None)

Per-cutout background mode: * 'local': subtract the median of stamp pixels that fall within sigma_clip_bg × std of the stamp median. This selects sky-like pixels (i.e. those not dominated by source flux) across the whole stamp rather than just the border ring. * None: no per-cutout subtraction (assumes image is already background-free).

'local' sigma_clip_bg float

Number of standard deviations from the stamp median used to define "sky" pixels. Default 3.0 (1-sigma clipping retains only the faint background pixels; increase to be more inclusive).

3.0 norm_mode ('catalog', 'measured', 'core')

How each stamp is flux-normalised before fitting: * 'catalog' (default): divide by the flux value in flux_col. * 'measured': divide by the sum of all finite, unmasked stamp pixels after background subtraction. Falls back to catalog flux when the measured sum is ≤ 0 or not finite. * 'core': divide by the sum of finite, unmasked pixels within a 3 px radius of the star centre. This avoids inflating the denominator with extended-wing flux and is more robust for PSFs with diffraction spikes. Falls back to catalog flux when the core sum is ≤ 0 or not finite.

'catalog'

Returns:

Name Type Description delta_col ndarray

Column offsets from star centre, shape (n_valid_stars, cutout_size²). Always fully populated (no NaN).

delta_row ndarray

Row offsets from star centre, shape (n_valid_stars, cutout_size²). Always fully populated (no NaN).

norm_flux ndarray

Normalised pixel fluxes pixel_flux / catalog_flux, shape (n_valid_stars, cutout_size²). Masked or bad pixels are NaN.

star_idx ndarray

1D integer array of shape (n_valid_stars,) mapping output row i to the row position of that star in selected_stars.

docs.title: evaluate_epsf
docs.text:
evaluate_epsf(
    model: PSFMachineModel,
    cutout_size: int | None = None,
    oversampling: int = 4,
    x_0: float = 0.0,
    y_0: float = 0.0,
    clip_negative: bool = False,
    normalise: bool = True,
) -> ndarray

Evaluate the ePSF model on an oversampled pixel grid.

The grid is centred at (x_0, y_0) (sub-pixel offset from the nearest detector pixel centre) and spans cutout_size native pixels in each dimension sampled at oversampling times the native pixel spacing. The evaluation covers the entire square pixel grid including all four corners.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model PSFMachineModel

Fitted B-spline ePSF model.

required cutout_size int or None

Stamp size in native detector pixels. Defaults to model.cutout_size if set on the model, otherwise 25.

None oversampling int

Oversampling factor (number of sub-pixels per native pixel). Default 4.

4 x_0 float

0.0 y_0 float

Sub-pixel offset of the star centre from the nearest pixel centre (in native pixels). Default (0, 0).

0.0 clip_negative bool

Set negative model values to zero. Default False (unnecessary when model.log_fit=True since 10^x > 0).

False normalise bool

Normalise the image so it sums to 1 on the native pixel grid (or to oversampling² on an oversampled grid before any renormalisation). Default True.

True

docs.title: fit_epsf
docs.text:
fit_epsf(
    delta_col: ndarray,
    delta_row: ndarray,
    norm_flux: ndarray,
    n_r_knots: int = 18,
    n_phi_knots: int = 15,
    rmin: float = 0.05,
    rmax: float | None = None,
    cut_r: float = 3.0,
    degree: int = 3,
    prior_sigma: float | None = 1000.0,
    norm_flux_err: ndarray | None = None,
    coords: str = "polar",
    n_col_knots: int | None = None,
    n_row_knots: int | None = None,
    log_fit: bool = False,
    cutout_size: int | None = None,
) -> PSFMachineModel

Fit a B-spline ePSF model to normalised pixel data.

Two coordinate systems are supported via coords:

"polar" (default) Fits a tensor-product model in (r, phi) polar coordinates. The radial basis uses clamped cubic B-splines on sqrt-spaced knots. The azimuthal basis uses periodic wrapped cubic B-splines. Inside cut_r only radial terms are active (no azimuthal modulation).

"cartesian" Fits a full 2D tensor-product model in (delta_col, delta_row). Knots are sqrt-spaced near the PSF core (within cut_r) for both axes, transitioning to linear spacing outside. The design matrix is the outer product of two 1D B-spline bases.

Inputs can be either 1D (n_pixels,) or 2D (n_stars, n_pixels_per_star) arrays (the output shape of :func:build_pixel_arrays). 2D inputs are ravelled internally before fitting.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default delta_col ndarray

Pixel offsets from star centres. Shape (n_pixels,) or (n_stars, n_pixels_per_star).

required delta_row ndarray

Pixel offsets from star centres. Shape (n_pixels,) or (n_stars, n_pixels_per_star).

required norm_flux ndarray

Normalised pixel fluxes. NaN values (masked pixels) are excluded automatically. Same shape as delta_col.

required n_r_knots int

Polar: number of radial knots (sqrt-spaced in [rmin, rmax]). Cartesian: number of knots per axis when n_col_knots / n_row_knots are not supplied. Default 24 (increased for sharp Roman WFI core).

18 n_phi_knots int

Number of azimuthal knots (polar mode only). Ignored for Cartesian. Default 15.

15 rmin float

Inner radial limit in detector pixels (polar mode). Default 0.05 (was 0.5 — reduced so the brightest center pixel is always fitted and evaluated rather than zeroed).

0.05 rmax float or None

Outer radial limit (polar) or domain half-width (Cartesian) in detector pixels. When None (default), auto-computed to cover the full input pixel grid including all four corners: sqrt(2) * (cutout_size/2 + 0.5) if cutout_size is known or inferred from 2D inputs, otherwise max(hypot(delta_col, delta_row)).

None cut_r float

Polar: radius inside which only radial terms are modelled. Cartesian: transition radius from sqrt-spaced to linear knots. Default 3.0.

3.0 degree int

B-spline degree. Default 3 (cubic).

3 prior_sigma float or None

Standard deviation of the zero-mean Gaussian prior on weights. Regularises the normal equations. Default 1000 (weak prior).

1000.0 norm_flux_err ndarray or None

Per-pixel uncertainties on norm_flux used as observation weights. Must have the same shape as norm_flux.

None coords str

Coordinate system: "polar" (default) or "cartesian".

'polar' n_col_knots int or None

Cartesian: number of column-axis knots. Defaults to n_r_knots.

None n_row_knots int or None

Cartesian: number of row-axis knots. Defaults to n_r_knots.

None log_fit bool

When False (default), fits directly in linear flux space. This preserves the arithmetic mean of the flux distribution and avoids Jensen's inequality underestimation in the core. When True, fit log₁₀(norm_flux). Pixels with norm_flux ≤ 0 are excluded automatically. :meth:~PSFMachineModel.evaluate transforms back to linear flux via 10 ** (A @ weights).

False cutout_size int or None

Stamp size in native detector pixels. When provided (or inferred from 2D delta_col input), saved in the model and used to auto-calculate rmax to cover the entire square grid including corners.

None

Returns:

Type Description PSFMachineModel

Fitted model. :attr:~PSFMachineModel.coords and :attr:~PSFMachineModel.log_fit record the fitting configuration so that :meth:~PSFMachineModel.evaluate and :func:evaluate_epsf automatically apply the correct transforms.

docs.title: refine_centroids
docs.text:
refine_centroids(
    model: PSFMachineModel,
    selected_stars: DataFrame,
    image: ndarray,
    dq: ndarray | None,
    cutout_size: int,
    flux_col: str | None = None,
    background: str | None = "local",
    sigma_clip_bg: float = 3.0,
    norm_mode: str = "catalog",
    core_radius: float = 3.0,
    max_shift: float = 2.0,
) -> tuple[DataFrame, ndarray, ndarray, ndarray, ndarray]

Update star centroid estimates by comparing each stamp to the current model.

For each star the model is evaluated on the stamp grid and the flux-weighted centroid of the residual is used to compute a shift. The x_pix/y_pix columns in selected_stars are updated in-place and the pixel arrays are rebuilt with the new centres so the result can be fed directly into the next :func:fit_epsf call.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model PSFMachineModel

Current best-fit ePSF model (e.g. from the previous iteration).

required selected_stars DataFrame

Star catalog with x_pix/y_pix columns.

required image ndarray

2D science image.

required dq ndarray or None

Data-quality array passed through to :func:build_pixel_arrays.

required cutout_size int

Stamp size in native pixels.

required flux_col str or None

Flux column name (forwarded to :func:build_pixel_arrays).

None background str or None

Background mode (forwarded to :func:build_pixel_arrays).

'local' sigma_clip_bg float

Sigma for background clipping (forwarded to :func:build_pixel_arrays).

3.0 norm_mode str

Normalisation mode (forwarded to :func:build_pixel_arrays).

'catalog' core_radius float

Aperture radius in native pixels within which data pixels are used to compute the centroid shift. Default 3.0. Restricting centroiding to the high-SNR core prevents faint outer wing noise and asymmetries from exerting lever-arm torque and smearing the ensemble core peak.

3.0 max_shift float

Maximum allowed centroid correction in native pixels. Larger shifts are clipped to avoid runaway corrections for blended/bad stars. Default 2.0.

2.0

Returns:

Name Type Description updated_stars DataFrame

Copy of selected_stars with updated x_pix/y_pix.

delta_col, delta_row, norm_flux, star_idx : np.ndarray

Pixel arrays rebuilt with the refined centres, ready for :func:fit_epsf.

docs.title: roman_epsf.psfmachine.io
docs.text:
FITS serialisation for :class:~roman_epsf.psfmachine.builder.PSFMachineModel.

FITS layout

save_model writes a two-extension FITS file:

  • PrimaryHDU — zero-size data; header holds all scalar parameters (RMIN, RMAX, CUT_R, NRKNOTS, NPHIKNOTS, DEGREE, NSTARS, NPIXELS) plus any caller-supplied extra keywords.
  • ImageHDU WEIGHTS — 1D float64 array of fitted spline coefficients.
  • ImageHDU R_KNOTS — 1D float64 array of radial knot positions.

save_image evaluates the model on an oversampled grid and writes a plain 2D ImageHDU with oversampling metadata in the header.

docs.title: Star Selection
docs.text: Utilities to select suitable stars for ePSF construction across Roman WFI detectors.

docs.title: roman_epsf.star_selection
docs.text:
Method-agnostic helpers for selecting point sources from a Roman WFI source catalog and extracting background-subtracted star cutouts suitable for any ePSF construction method.

These utilities are intentionally decoupled from the photutils submodule so that future ePSF method modules (e.g. WebbPSF, pixel-convolution) can reuse the same star-selection and extraction logic.

docs.title: extract_star_cutouts
docs.text:
extract_star_cutouts(
    image: ndarray,
    dq: ndarray | None,
    selected_stars: DataFrame,
    cutout_size: int,
    snr_threshold: float = 5.0,
    min_snr_pixels: int = 5,
    background: str | None = "global",
    bkg2d_kwargs: dict | None = None,
) -> tuple[NDData, EPSFStars, DataFrame, float]

Extract background-subtracted star cutouts for ePSF construction.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default image ndarray

2D detector science image.

required dq ndarray or None

2D data-quality array. Bits DO_NOT_USE and SATURATED are masked when roman-datamodels is installed; otherwise all non-zero DQ values are masked.

required selected_stars DataFrame

Star catalog with x_pix and y_pix columns (output of :func:select_stars).

required cutout_size int

Stamp size in pixels (should be odd for EPSFBuilder).

required snr_threshold float

Minimum per-pixel SNR for a cutout to be considered valid.

5.0 min_snr_pixels int

Minimum number of pixels above snr_threshold required to keep a cutout.

5 background ('global', '2d', None)

Background subtraction mode:

  • 'global' – subtract a single sigma-clipped median scalar (astropy.stats.sigma_clipped_stats).
  • '2d' – fit and subtract a 2D background surface (photutils.background.Background2D). Pass bkg2d_kwargs to control box_size, filter_size, sigma_clip, etc.
  • None / 'none' – no background subtraction.
'global' bkg2d_kwargs dict or None

Keyword arguments forwarded to photutils.background.Background2D when background='2d'. Ignored for other modes.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description nddata NDData

Background-subtracted, bad-pixel-masked image wrapped for photutils.psf.extract_stars.

stars EPSFStars

Valid star cutouts ready for EPSFBuilder.

filtered_df DataFrame

Subset of selected_stars corresponding to the returned cutouts.

background_std float

RMS of the background estimate (scalar sigma for 'global', median RMS for '2d', or NaN when background is None).
